Ganjikunta is a notable mountain pass located in the Eastern Ghats

• Location: Eastern Ghats, connecting sections between the Seshachalam and Nallamala hill ranges.

• Function: Acts as a geographical break dividing parts of the uplands and lowlands in the region.

• Terrain: Characterized by dry deciduous forests and rocky elevations typical of peninsular India's eastern hill ranges.

sheets.heading: Major Forest Types
sheets.text:
Major Forest Types

A. Moist Deciduous Forests

• Receives maximum rainfall

• Forests in AP are predominantly deciduous forests.

B. Dry Deciduous Forests

• Rainfall: 75–100 cm

• Associated with the relatively drier parts of AP.

• A major dry-deciduous forest belt occurs around the Seshachalam–Nallamala hill system. The long Eastern Ghats pass through the dry deciduous forests of Seshachalam and Nallamala.

C. Short Thorn Forests

• Rainfall: \<70 cm

• Characteristic of the driest areas of AP.

D. Tidal Forests

• Mangrove trees

• Also called Koringa forests

• Located at the faces/mouths of Krishna and Godavari rivers.
